summary: Three-stage layout animation driver owned by a UI window: a stage byte plus three embedded 0x50-byte Ui_AnimShake sub-animations that run one after another, a two-entry child delegate array and a tween block at +0x2A0.
evidence: Ui_AnimSequence_Update (0x0021FBC4) switches on the state byte at +0x49 and drives the three 0x50-byte shake blocks at +0x4C/+0x9C/+0xEC through Ui_AnimShake_Update (0x003E021C) and func_00649B80; Ui_AnimSequence_Reset (0x0021FC90) resets +0x49 and the first shake block. The child list at +0x278 is walked to +0x280 and +0x2BC is set to &self[0x2C0].

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: Ui_AnimSequence_Update switches on this byte (0/1/2/3) and Ui_AnimSequence_Reset sets it to 0, so it is the index of the running animation stage.

fields.name: shakeA
fields.evidence: Embedded Ui_AnimShake (0x50 bytes): Ui_AnimSequence_Update calls Ui_AnimShake_Update(&self->f_4c, 0) and func_003DFEC4/func_00649B80 on it. The next two sub-animations follow at +0x9C and +0xEC, exactly 0x50 bytes apart.

fields.name: shakeB
fields.evidence: Second embedded Ui_AnimShake: stage 1 of Ui_AnimSequence_Update only calls func_003DFEC4(&self->f_9c); Ui_AnimShake_Update(&self->f_9c, 1) starts it from stage 0.

fields.name: shakeC
fields.evidence: Third embedded Ui_AnimShake: stage 2 of Ui_AnimSequence_Update calls func_003DFEC4(&self->f_ec) and func_00649B80(&self->f_ec) and then moves to stage 3.

fields.name: children
fields.evidence: Two-entry delegate array walked by maybe_Ui_AnimSequence_UpdateChildren (0x00422164): `for (puVar3 = self+0x278; puVar3 != self+0x280; puVar3++)` dereferences each entry and calls its vtable slots +0x24 (reset) and +0x28 (update).

fields.name: maybe_currentChildId
fields.evidence: Compared with 0xFFFF and written back as 0xFFFF when the child reports completion (`*(short *)(param_1 + 0x280) = (short)0xFFFF`), so 0xFFFF is the 'no child' sentinel.

fields.name: maybe_tween
fields.evidence: self+0x2A0: passed to FUN_003F7718; its extent is not recovered, so it is sized to the next known field at +0x2BC rather than overrunning it

fields.name: currentChild
fields.evidence: self+0x2BC: written with &self[0x2C0], so it is a pointer into the embedded child slot at +0x2C0

fields.name: maybe_childSlot
fields.evidence: self+0x2C0: the embedded object that the pointer at +0x2BC points at; its own layout is not recovered

summary: Battle command queue (the generated name Ui_CmdQueue is wrong): a per-frame array of five 0x8C-byte command slots that the battle action producers push into and the per-frame processor drains into the battle action list.
evidence: Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry (0x0016B810) writes the frame header at self->f_e8 + frame*0x2C8 (+0x2BC stored value, +0x2C0 battle-RNG roll, +0x2C4 mode byte, +0x2C5 flag), copies the widget into slot*0x8C and writes the event id at +0x88, then increments the frame index at self+0x124 when slot 0 is used. Callers are the battle action producers (Battle_Update, Battle_ExecuteItemAction, Battle_QueueAbilityAction, Battle_SelectAiActions), so the generated name Ui_CmdQueue is misleading.

fields.name: maybe_widgetContext
fields.evidence: &self->f_b4 is passed as the first argument to the per-event factory table at 0x007A4338 / 0x007A4268 (`(**(code **)(0x007A4338 + id*4))(&self->f_b4, self, id)`), so +0xB4 is an embedded context object, not a pointer.

fields.name: maybe_payloadHeader
fields.evidence: Copied into the first word of every command payload before Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry / Battle_WriteActionSlot (`local_4c = self->f_b8`), so it is a per-queue header value stamped on each queued command.

fields.name: frames
fields.evidence: self->f_e8: base of the per-frame array, stride 0x2C8, five 0x8C-byte command slots per frame

fields.name: maybe_forceProcessFlag
fields.evidence: Ui_CmdQueue_ProcessSlots (0x0016932C) tests +0xFB to bypass the widget-active (i[4]==0) check and to allow the 0x549 command rewrite, i.e. it forces processing of the queued slot

fields.name: pendingList
fields.evidence: Intrusive list head: func_001235A4(&self->f_10c, &self->f_10c, node) appends the widget created for each processed slot.

fields.name: maybe_lastSlotValue
fields.evidence: Set to the +0x70 word of the slot just processed (`self->f_118 = *(u32*)(slot + 0x70)`), i.e. the sequence value that was stored into that slot.

fields.name: sequenceCounter
fields.evidence: Clamped to >= 1, incremented per queued command and written into slot+0x70, so it is the monotonic command sequence number.

fields.name: frameIndex
fields.evidence: self->f_124: frame index, incremented after a push into slot 0 and decremented for the other slots

summary: Fade/wipe helper owned by the map window: two screen objects it fades in and out, plus a five-slot ring of icon sprites that trail the last cursor position.
evidence: Ui_FadeWipe_Init (0x00621874) writes the two screen objects at self+0x130/+0x134, keeps the last icon position at self+0x1A0..+0x1A8, stores five 0x10-byte icon slots at self+0x1AC and wraps the ring index at self+0x1FC (reset to 0 when it exceeds 4). Callers Ui_MapWindow_BindPanes (0x00620BA8) and Ui_MapWindow_SetIconVisibility (0x0062155C) place it in the map window. The batch's offsets 0x14/0x30/0x40/0x50/0x60/0x70/0xC0 are accesses on `params` or on the screen objects in the same body, so they are kept as unknown rather than given an invented purpose.

evidence: maybe_Ui_ToggleLabel_SetState (0x002D20F4) calls func_001A5C78 on the embedded objects at self+0x140 and self+0x1FC, then writes the same state byte into self+0x1A8 and self+0x1E0 (the +4 byte of the objects at +0x1A4 and +0x1DC), so the class is two symmetric halves switched by one state value.

summary: 3D background of the profile window: a field-object handle, two generation-tagged pack handles with their state words, and the embedded view/child objects.
evidence: Ui_3DBackground_DtorBody (0x00463B34) re-installs vtable 0x00771DD4, frees the pack handles at self+0x310 and self+0x318 (index in the low 12 bits, generation in the high bits, checked against 0x000FFFFF), clears the state words at +0x30C/+0x314, releases the field-object handle at +0x2E8 through func_001C7570 and calls SetupView(self, 0).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: `*self = 0x00771DD4` in Ui_3DBackground_DtorBody; vtable 0x00771DD4 has 10 slots including maybe_Ui_3DBackground_Init and Ui_3DBackground_DeletingDtor.

fields.name: unknown_word_130
fields.evidence: Artifact: the evidence `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x4c))(param_1)` is a vtable slot call, scaled by 4.

fields.name: fieldObjectHandle

fields.name: packState0

fields.name: packHandle0

fields.name: packState1

fields.name: packHandle1

summary: Small float shake/tween attached to a layout element: a target object, the current value, two target values and a signed velocity that flips when the target is reached.
evidence: Ui_AnimShake_Update (0x003E021C) returns early when +0x14 is null or +0x2C is 0.0, stores the two float arguments into +0x44/+0x48 (the second may be -1.0, replaced by a random value), copies +0x44 into the current value at +0x18, sets the changed flag at +0x1C and negates +0x2C into the signed velocity at +0x4C.

fields.name: target
fields.evidence: Every routine returns immediately when this is 0; maybe_Ui_AnimShake_Update passes self+8 to func_0065D3B8/func_0065D38C and Ui_LayoutElement_SetTargetValue, so it is the animated object.

fields.name: currentValue
fields.evidence: self->f_18: assigned the x target (+0x44) every update - the value the shake drives

fields.name: isDirty
fields.evidence: self->f_1c: set to 1 after an update when the target at +0x14 is non-null

fields.name: speed
fields.evidence: self->f_2c: a 0.0 value disables the shake, and it is negated into the velocity at +0x4C when the target is reached

fields.name: targetX
fields.evidence: self->f_44: first float argument, copied into the current value at +0x18

fields.name: targetY
fields.evidence: self->f_48: second float argument; -1.0 is a sentinel replaced by a random value from func_0065D3B8(self + 8)

fields.name: velocity
fields.evidence: self->f_4c: assigned -speed (+0x2C) each time the current value reaches the target, so it is the signed step direction
